subject.title: [Bug]: sessions_yield subagent wake can compact parent branch at low context usage

question: Should compaction entries gain a closed trigger/cause field, and should successful-turn overflow decisions require contextUsage or last-call sanity instead of aggregate billing usage during subagent wake?
rationale: The bug is real, but the durable fix affects transcript schema, audit semantics, Codex usage interpretation, and session wake behavior, which are product and compatibility contracts rather than a purely mechanical edit.

options.title: Add trigger metadata and guard overflow
options.body: Add a closed compaction reason field plus a successful-turn overflow guard based on trusted context snapshots or last-call usage, then require focused current-main live proof.

options.title: Guard overflow first
options.body: Fix the spurious overflow predicate now and defer transcript trigger metadata to a follow-up schema/API decision.

options.title: Keep current mitigation pending live repro
options.body: Leave the current contextUsage mitigation as-is until maintainers reproduce the subagent-yield failure on current main.

recommendation.title: Add trigger metadata and guard overflow
recommendation.body: Add a closed compaction reason field plus a successful-turn overflow guard based on trusted context snapshots or last-call usage, then require focused current-main live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision mostly concerns usage accounting and session compaction semantics, where this history signal is stronger than the package-split blame.
